clue.text: He plants the vegetables right and brings them forward

definitions.text: He plants the vegetables right and brings them forward

parts.note: farm produce is vegetables and fruit grown for sale

explanation.surface: A gardener sows his vegetable crop properly and brings it on early.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it defines a grower who sets out his crops and also yields PRODUCE (the vegetables) followed by R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A grower who raises crops and brings them to market is a maker of goods in the farming sense.

clue.text: Kinsman found to be an unpleasant oriental

indicators.note: unpleasant suggests the letters of the following word are made nasty, that is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a family member is a disagreeable Easterner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpleasant' looks like a description of the person but signals rearranging the letters of ORIENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a family member, someone connected by blood.

clue.text: In low spirits because record was played well into the night

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record that is playing is on
so late means at a very advanced hour

explanation.surface: Someone feels miserable because a record was played noisily far into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dejected and unconsoled is the same as being in a gloomy mood.

clue.text: Man follows the idiot, to dress him

indicators.note: follows places the man's pronoun after the word for the idiot

parts.note: clot is British slang for a fool
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man comes after a fool to help him get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone is to put garments on them.

clue.text: Scold a supporter of public transport

definitions.meaning: to complain or rant at someone
a train runs on steel tracks that bear its weight

explanation.definitionFit: To rant bitterly is to scold; a steel bar of track bears up trains.

clue.text: Colour sergeant taking part in Spanish dance

parts.note: flame is a bright orange-red colour
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A colour sergeant joins in a dance in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour sergeant' is a real army rank, but here it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian dance style with guitar and stamping.

clue.text: It's made by a dog on a tree

definitions.meaning: the outer covering of a trunk

explanation.definitionFit: A dog's woof has the same name as the rough outer skin of a trunk.

clue.text: Shows parts of the face

definitions.meaning: to feature something is to show or present it
the nose, eyes and mouth are facial elements

explanation.definitionFit: A film features (presents) its stars; nose, eyes and mouth are one's facial elements.

clue.text: Place where you might hear a Londoner greeting Catherine

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H of hello, giving 'allo
Cate is a short form of the name Catherine

explanation.surface: A spot where a Cockney might be heard saying hello to Catherine.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney (working-class Londoner) traditionally drops initial H, so 'hello' becomes 'allo.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to assign or position something, to give it its spot.

clue.text: Took the unfinished salad back, unfortunately

indicators.note: back tells us to read the shortened salad in the opposite direction
unfinished means the word salad loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone sadly took a half-eaten salad back to the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' trims salad to SALA; 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used like sadly.

clue.text: Stock exchange perhaps

parts.note: not the place where shares are traded: here stock means livestock, and exchange is where the animals are bought and sold

explanation.definitionFit: Livestock is traded at a farmers' auction venue for cows.

clue.text: Derisory applause on failure, but given a nice spread

indicators.note: on places the second piece after the first

parts.note: a raspberry is a rude noise blown to mock someone
a jam is a stoppage or breakdown of a machine

explanation.surface: A performer is mocked when things go wrong, but still enjoys a generous feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit preserve made from red berries is a pleasant topping for toast.

clue.text: European rival at one point seen around

parts.note: to vie is to compete with, to rival
N, north, is one point of the compass

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of the word seen are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A competitor from the Continent is spotted at some moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals that SEEN is mixed to make NESE; N is north on the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Vienna, the Austrian capital, is a Continental.

clue.text: In story 100 return to applause

indicators.note: return means the combined letters are read backwards
In indicates that the Roman hundred goes inside the word for a story

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: In a tale, a hundred people come back to give an ovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means brilliant success or acclaim, a burst of public praise.

clue.text: Greek hero got no rest, unhappily

indicators.note: unhappily suggests the words no rest are upset and put out of order

explanation.surface: A warrior of Greece found no peace, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges the letters of NO REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor was the wise old king of Pylos who fought at Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Shortened knowledge put in plain form

indicators.note: put in says the letters sit inside the words plain form, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Abbreviated facts are written out in simple terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' looks like an instruction to rewrite, but the letters sit inside 'plain form'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped colloquial word for information is knowledge cut short.

clue.text: Example in position

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: An illustration of something being in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A case or illustration of something is a specimen of it.

clue.text: Volley fired with some colossal volume

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Guns let loose a barrage with enormous noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of shots.

clue.text: Hide with cunning, but not far below the surface

parts.note: hide is an animal's skin
deep can mean artful or crafty, as in a deep one

explanation.surface: Someone conceals something cleverly, though only just out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Superficial things go no further than the outer layer.

clue.text: Man in charge of the stud

definitions.meaning: the person who runs things at work
a raised knob or ornamental stud on a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the head at work; a raised knob is an ornamental stud.

clue.text: RA statue smashed by soak

indicators.note: smashed suggests the statue is broken to pieces, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Royal Academy statue is broken by a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a noun for a drunk, but it is the verb meaning drench. RA is the Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench something thoroughly is to fill it with liquid.

clue.text: Expedition was as fair as could be

indicators.note: could be implies the words as fair might become something else, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trip was as pleasant as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as could be' reads as an intensifier, but 'could be' rearranges AS FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is a journey, typically in Africa, to see or hunt wild animals.

clue.text: Allow for real flexibility in transport

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for carrying

parts.note: to tote is to carry or transport

indicators.note: flexibility tells us the word real bends into a different order

explanation.surface: Permit some real give in the travel arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is a verb here: to tote is to carry. 'flexibility' bends REAL into LERA.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to permit it.

clue.text: Call to see the inside

explanation.definitionFit: To pay a short visit and to peer within share one phrase.

clue.text: A very quiet finish, in the city, to my operation

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly
an end is a finish
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Something quiet ends my surgery in town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode area of the City, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: The removal of the appendix is a surgical procedure.

clue.text: Stiff, but with a soft edge

parts.note: p, piano, means soft in music
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Something rigid, but with a gentle border.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means formal and starchy in manner.

clue.text: Fish for tea perhaps

definitions.meaning: British slang for tea, from the Chinese word cha

explanation.definitionFit: Arctic char is a salmon-family fish; char is old British slang for a cuppa.

clue.text: French man or English lady

explanation.definitionFit: The same first name is masculine in France and feminine in Britain.

clue.text: Got me a chair-or was that just a flight of fancy?

indicators.note: got here is read as 'got into shape', telling us the words me a chair are reorganised

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they have been given a seat, then doubts it was real.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimaera is an imagined monster, so the word means a fanciful dream or illusion.

clue.text: Recount story about the anaesthetic

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a number is something that numbs, as an anaesthetic does

explanation.surface: Retell a tale about an anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, something that deadens feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To count again is to assign figures afresh.
